headline: MCA reportedly proposes CSR framework overhaul: wider Schedule VII, stricter NGO norms
summary_points: MCA has reportedly proposed a major overhaul of the CSR framework, per a report by A2Z Taxcorp LLP.
Reported proposals include an expanded Schedule VII list of eligible CSR activities.
Stricter registration norms for NGOs implementing CSR projects are reportedly proposed.
New restrictions on use of CSR funds and a voluntary impact assessment are also reported; details are unconfirmed.
who_is_affected: Companies covered by Section 135 of the Companies Act, CSR implementing agencies and NGOs, and professionals advising on CSR compliance.
action_required: Await the official MCA draft or notification, verify the actual proposals and comment timelines, and review current CSR policies and NGO partners accordingly.

social.linkedin:
MCA has reportedly proposed a significant overhaul of the CSR framework, according to a report by A2Z Taxcorp LLP.

The reported proposals include:
- An expanded Schedule VII list of eligible activities
- Stricter registration norms for NGOs implementing CSR projects
- New restrictions on the use of CSR funds
- A voluntary impact assessment

The report is based on a press source and the detailed text of the proposal is not yet available to us, so specifics such as the scope of changes, timelines and effective dates remain unconfirmed.

For companies under Section 135, this could affect CSR policy design, project selection and the vetting of implementing partners. NGOs may also need to prepare for tighter registration and compliance requirements.

CAs, CSs and finance teams may want to track the official MCA release and any consultation window so that comments and policy updates can be planned in time.

Please verify the details with the official MCA source before acting.
